newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-ENGLAND, NZ FIRST TEST EVENLY BALANCED.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ENGLAND, NZ FIRST TEST EVENLY BALANCED.

text.p: The first cricket test between England and New Zealand was evenly balanced after the third day's play at Eden Park on Sunday.
In reply to New Zealand's first innings 390, England were 366 for six at the close, with left-hander Graham Thorpe on 57 and Dominic Cork on 16.
The day belonged to England's wicketkeeper-batsman Alec Stewart and captain Mike Atherton, who shared a 182-run stand in 377 balls for the second wicket.
Atherton fought his way back into the runs after a lean tour with a gritty 83 while Stewart made his 10th test century -- and his fourth against New Zealand -- scoring 173.
Stewart batted 364 minutes, faced 277 balls and hit 23 boundaries and one six.
England lost their way in the final session. John Crawley was run out by the length of the pitch after a mix up with Thorpe, and Craig White went leg before wicket on the next ball.
Thorpe had completed his 20th test half century, having batted 3-1/2 hours.
Simon Doull and offspinner Dipak Patel were the pick of the New Zealand attack, with two wickets apiece.
